agree.reason: It's a warm, clear letter that a quick reader would take as a solid recommendation, but it leaves out the $8,000 saving, the part-time job held open during the program and the offer to take a call, so it reads like many of the other 150 letters.

honest.reason: Several claims aren't in the facts: that 'nobody required him' to learn the software, that he deals with equipment problems before the crew arrives, that he works on weaknesses 'without being asked', and that his father was 'seriously' ill.

works_the_facts.reason: The facts allow two stronger figures, but the letter uses neither: about 780 solo 3 a.m. shifts with 2 missed (better than 99.7% attendance), and the vet's estimate that the nine early mastitis catches saved about $8,000.

right_comparison.reason: Nothing sets Tomás against the typical applicant or a typical young farm worker, so the reader has no baseline for how unusual unsupervised night responsibility and catching cases from herd data are.

qualification.reason: The written-English caveat is hedged without anything the reader can check, such as when the night class ends, his progress so far, or that he failed and then passed the written safety test, so the committee can't judge the risk for coursework.

objections.reason: It raises the absence and the written-English concern, but on the absence it leaves out the answers it had: he arranged his cousin to cover his shifts and came back on the day he said. It also never addresses whether he can stay employed through the program, even though his job is being held open part-time.

fit.reason: It's the right length and form for a one-page manager's letter, but it still has placeholders for the farm name, the manager's name, Tomás's surname and the phone number, which the writer was able to get.
